full_judgment: 40. In the case of Nawab Ali Dhakua vs. Abdur Rahman & others reported in 1994 BLD (AD) 229 leave was granted on the ground that the High Court Division in affirming the finding of possession of the trial Court did not itself discuss the evidence of possession and come to any independent finding of its own but simply agreed with that of the trial Court. The learned Counsel for the appellant referring to the provision of Order XLI, rule 31 submitted that the High Court Division failed to discuss independently the evidence of possession given by the plaintiffs and further gave no elaborate reasons for discarding the same but merely approved the finding of the trial Court that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession and that a trial Court should not be treated as infallible only because it saw and heard the witnesses and as the appellate Court has jurisdiction to review the evidence in order to determine whether the conclusion originally reached on that evidence should stand and in support of the above contention the learned Counsel cited the opinion of Viscount Simpon in Watt vs Thomas (1947) 1 All ER 582. The learned Counsel for the respondent, on the other hand, referred to the decision reported in AIR 1967 SC 1124.
